Test Description: Verify that the public homepage opens successfully and exposes its primary page content and Login navigation.
Preconditions: Apache is running; the application is available at http://localhost/barbershop-1/; no authenticated session is active.
Test Steps: 1. Open the application URL; 2. Verify the navigation response is successful; 3. Verify the page body is visible; 4. Verify the Login link is visible.
Expected Result: The server returns a successful HTTP response, the page body is visible, and the Login link is visible.
Actual Result: Codex-verified Chromium execution passed all assertions. Test duration: 3.7 seconds; overall one-test run: 6.5 seconds.
Remarks: Separate historical result: the user reported a successful Chromium run of approximately 1.5 seconds on the same date.

Test Description: Verify that a registered regular user can sign in with valid credentials.
Preconditions: Apache and MySQL are running; the application database is available; a dedicated non-sensitive QA user exists; the user is logged out.
Test Steps: 1. Open the homepage; 2. Select Login; 3. Enter the QA user's Email Address; 4. Enter the QA user's Password; 5. Select Login; 6. Verify navigation to index.php; 7. Verify the authenticated profile control and Logout link.
Test Data: Dedicated QA account supplied through the ignored local .env file; password intentionally omitted from documentation.
Expected Result: The user is authenticated, redirected to index.php, shown the profile control and Logout action, and no longer shown the public Login link.
Actual Result: Codex-verified Chromium execution passed all authentication and account-interface assertions. Test duration: 4.7 seconds; overall one-test run: 5.5 seconds.
Remarks: A dedicated dummy QA account was created after explicit approval. Account identity fields are masked in screenshot evidence; no password is committed or displayed.

Test Description: Verify that an authenticated regular user can log out and that the authenticated session is terminated.
Preconditions: Apache and MySQL are running; the application database is available; a dedicated QA account exists; the user is authenticated and the profile control is visible.
Test Steps: 1. Log in with the dedicated QA account; 2. Open the authenticated profile menu; 3. Select Logout; 4. Verify the logout process completes and redirects to index.php; 5. Verify the public Login link is visible; 6. Verify the authenticated profile control is absent.
Test Data: Dedicated QA account supplied through the ignored local .env file; password intentionally omitted from documentation.
Expected Result: The session is destroyed, the browser returns to index.php, the public Login link is visible, and authenticated profile controls are no longer available.
Remarks: Planned test. Logout clears the PHP session and redirects to index.php after the application's logout transition.
